record.description: NFC Forum-compliant controller with an integrated Arm Cortex-M0 running NXP's NFC stack, exposing an NCI interface over I2C to the host; reader/writer, card emulation and P2P; 13.56 MHz; one antenna path. p.1 title verbatim: 'High performance NFC controller with integrated firmware, supporting all NFC Forum modes'.
record.description_quote: High performance NFC controller with integrated firmware, supporting all NFC Forum modes

record.rails_why: VBAT accepts 2.3–5.5 V and VDD(PAD) has a '3 V host supply' option at 3.0–3.6 V (Table 26), so a single 3.3 V rail powers both the chip and its host interface toward the Radxa.
record.absolute_max: p.43 Table 25 'Limiting values' — 'In accordance with the Absolute Maximum Rating System (IEC 60134).' Rows verbatim: 'VDD(PAD) VDD(PAD) supply voltage supply voltage for host - 4.35 V'; 'VBAT battery supply voltage - 6 V'; 'Ptot total power dissipation all modes - 600 mW'; 'Tstg storage temperature -55 +150 °C'.

supplies.name: VBAT
supplies.cite: p.44 Table 26 'Operating conditions', rows verbatim: 'VBAT battery supply voltage battery monitor enabled;VSS = [1][1] 2.3 - 5.5 V' and 'Reader, Active Initiator 2.7 - 5.5 V' (the 'and Active Target;VSS = 0 V' continuation on the next line). 2.7 V is carried as v_min because reader mode is what a tag-reading robot uses; card-emulation / passive-target may run from 2.3 V. TYP column is '-' — null by observation.

supplies.name: VDD(PAD)
supplies.cite: p.44 Table 26 rows verbatim: '• 1.8 V host supply;VSS = 0 V 1.65 1.8 1.95 V' and '• 3 V host supply;VSS = 0 V 3.0 - 3.6 V'. The 3 V option is carried (Radxa header logic is 3.3 V); the 1.8 V option exists.

record.interface_cite: §12.3.1 'I2C-bus interface'; the maximum clock is in '16.2.5 I2C-bus timings' (p.47), not transcribed — null, not a guess.
record.i2c_address_why: SELECTABLE BY TWO PINS, base not transcribed: pin table verbatim 'I2CADR0 1 I VDD(PAD) I C-bus address 0' and 'I2CADR1 3 I VDD(PAD) I C-bus address 1' (HVQFN40 pins 1 and 3). The resulting 7-bit addresses are in §12.3.1.1 'I2C-bus configuration' (p.22), unread. The Microduck's I2C3 already carries 0x18, 0x19/0x68 and 0x29 — a design must pick a strap that avoids those.

standards_claimed.cite: table of contents §12.7.2 and §12.7.3.1 as extracted; plus the title's 'supporting all NFC Forum modes'. Vendor claims of protocol compliance; nothing here verifies them.

pinout.$about: NOT TRANSCRIBED beyond the two I2C address pins above. §11.1 'Pinning HVQFN40' (p.11) holds the 40-pin map.

unknowns: THE FITTED NFC IC IN THE MICRODUCK: CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §8). This is a candidate.

ONE ANTENNA PATH: the PN7150 drives one antenna (TX1/TX2, RXN/RXP); two antennas (head + beak) would need two controllers or an RF switch — the sheet does not discuss switching. The ST25R3916 candidate states two single-ended antenna drives.
Reader-mode current (§16.1), I2C timing (§16.2.5), I2C base address (§12.3.1.1) and the full pin map (§11.1) not transcribed.

Firmware code variant 'xx' in PN7150B0HN/C110xx: the sheet's §3 notes /C11006 'contains a firmware update compared to the previous version' and /C11004 'has been withdrawn' — which variant to order is a live question the product page would settle.
